summary: Verified new storage_path feature on /api/doc-uploads/ (supervision uploads). Wrote pytest suite (8 tests, all passing) covering: DOCX + PDF upload persist file to storage BEFORE background AI task; download endpoint returns byte-identical file with correct filename/content-type; 403 for attendee role; 403 for attendee upload; 404 for nonexistent upload_id (download & delete); delete removes DB row + best-effort storage cleanup; full AI lifecycle (processing -> text_ready -> done, evidence PUT still works). Frontend spot-checked: DocUploadReport.js shows 'Download original' button (data-testid=download-upload-btn) next to 'View portfolio' — button is visible, click handler wired, and existing ComplianceTab evidence view renders as before.

integration_issues.issue: Uploads created BEFORE m015 migration have storage_path=NULL, so clicking 'Download original' returns 404 (silent console error, no user-visible toast/alert). Not a regression — the file legitimately doesn't exist for those rows — but consider hiding the button (or showing a disabled 'Original file not available' state) when upload.storage_path is null / for uploads created before the migration date. New uploads work perfectly.

action_items: Optional UX polish: gray out / hide the Download original button when upload.storage_path is null (legacy uploads from before m015). Currently the button is always shown, and legacy uploads produce a silent 404 + console error on click.
Consider surfacing download errors to the user (toast/alert) instead of only console.error — right now handleDownload() swallows failures silently.
critical_code_review_comments: doc_uploads.py:107-113 — put_document() failure is swallowed and actual_path set to None, meaning the DB row is still created with storage_path=NULL and the upload proceeds. Users would only find out at download time. Acceptable per current design (background AI still runs), but worth logging a warning-severity error visible in ops.

doc_uploads.py:296-300 — delete_document() error is caught and only logged; DB row is already deleted so orphan file is possible on storage-provider outage. Matches the standards_documents pattern per spec, but this is best-effort, not guaranteed cleanup.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (button renders + click wired; legacy-upload 404 is data-state, not a bug)

context_for_next_testing_agent: test_supervision_upload_storage.py requires REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL env var (pytest.ini uses xdist so run with `cd /app/backend && REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL=https://supervision-preview.preview.emergentagent.com python -m pytest tests/test_supervision_upload_storage.py -v`). Manager MFA was NOT enforced this session (login returned no mfa_required) — if future test agents hit MFA, use the get_tokens.py helper documented in /app/memory/test_credentials.md. The 'cross-org 404' case from the review request is covered indirectly by the org-scoped WHERE clause (all queries include AND org_id=$2); a dedicated multi-org test would need a second seeded org and was not written this iteration.
rca of the issue: N/A — no bugs found. The one integration observation (legacy uploads produce silent 404 on download) is expected behavior given the migration was additive (m015 only adds the column; it doesn't backfill files that never existed) and is a UX-polish suggestion, not a regression.
